narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To persuade viewers that the world is becoming more peaceful over the long term, encouraging support for peace and democracy despite current conflicts.

units.meaning: The data series is annual battle deaths per million people, covering 1950 through 2010.
accepted_routes: Annual battle deaths per million people, 1950–2010
The metric is battle deaths per million, tracked yearly from 1950 to 2010
A six-decade series of battle deaths per million population
units.visual_evidence_rule: The data trace must be identified as battle deaths per million people and must cover 1950 through 2010.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly identify the metric as battle deaths per million people rather than total battle deaths?

units.meaning: Long-term downward trend: battle deaths per million is much lower at the end of the series in 2010 than at the start in 1950.
accepted_routes: Battle deaths per million fell from about 180 in 1950 to about 12 in 2010
The long-run direction is downward over the six decades
The 2010 level is far below the 1950 level
units.visual_evidence_rule: The data trace from 1950 to 2010 must show a net decrease from the first value to the last value.
units.reviewer_question: Is the net 1950-to-2010 decline sufficient to convey long-term peace, or must intermediate years also be emphasized?

units.meaning: The size of the 1950-to-2010 decline: 167.9 fewer battle deaths per million, about 93% lower than 1950.
accepted_routes: A drop of about 168 battle deaths per million
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must make the 1950 and 2010 endpoints visible or annotate the derived decline.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the decline, or is showing the downward shape enough?

units.meaning: Early steep decline: battle deaths per million fell from 180.2 in 1950 to 20.5 in 1955, a drop of 159.7 and about 89% below 1950.
accepted_routes: By 1955 the rate was about 89% below 1950
The early 1950s saw a steep fall, from 180.2 to 20.5
Battle deaths per million dropped sharply between 1950 and 1955
units.visual_evidence_rule: The data trace must show a sharp decrease between 1950 and 1955.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video call out the early 1950s decline, or focus only on the full-period trend?

units.meaning: The decline is not monotonic: after the early drop, temporary rebounds occurred, including 48.6 in 1973 and 42.1 in 1984, before later decline.

basis.note: comparison to show rebounds remain below the start

accepted_routes: The decline was interrupted by rebounds, including 48.6 in 1973 and 42.1 in 1984
The series is not a smooth downward line
There were later peaks in the 1970s and 1980s, though both stayed below the 1950 level
units.visual_evidence_rule: The data trace must show local highs around 1973 and 1984 rather than a smooth uninterrupted decline.
units.temporal_anchor: Yes, there are nasty conflicts going on in many places
units.reviewer_question: Must the video acknowledge temporary reversals/rebounds, or can it simplify to the net downward trend?

optional_valid: The highest value in the table is 180.2 battle deaths per million in 1950.
The lowest value in the table is 9.5 battle deaths per million, occurring in 1961 and 1998.
The 2010 value is 12.3 battle deaths per million, which is not the series minimum.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims that democracy causes peace or that speaking up directly reduces battle deaths.
Extrapolating beyond 2010 or claiming the world will become completely peaceful.
Using total battle deaths or absolute counts; the table unit is deaths per million.
Calling 2010 the lowest value; 1961 and 1998 are lower at 9.5.
Referring to current conflicts after 2010 as if they were in the data.
Claiming all conflicts have ended or that battle deaths are zero.
notes: The core required story is a long-run decline in battle deaths per million from 1950 to 2010, but the table also shows an early steep drop and later rebounds. Optional units make the non-monotonicity visible without overstating the data.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
